title: add-tenant-headroom-sentinel-and-adaptive-rollback-quanta
author: Aisha Khanna
description: Context: Recent rollouts exposed a pattern where a small subset of tenants with bursty traffic exhausted replica headroom and caused noisy tail latency regressions that standard canaries missed (because aggregate signals were dominated by stable tenants). This PR introduces a tenant-aware headroom sentinel that synthesizes low-sample microburst probes, maintains per-tenant capacity fingerprints, and computes an adaptive rollback quantum so rollouts can fail fast for affected tenants while continuing elsewhere. Motivation: reduce blast radius of perf regressions caused by tenant-specific workload modes and improve sensitivity for sparse high-impact tenants without increasing false positives for the majority. Summary of changes: - Add headroom estimator + fingerprint store with eviction and time-decay (canary/orchestrator/headroom_sentinel.py) - Implement microburst synthetic probe that targets short-window concurrency saturation (canary/probes/microburst_probe.go) - Integrate sentinel with rollout controller to emit per-tenant "quanta" decisions (canary/orchestrator/rollback_quanta.go) - Small TS/JS bindings for Console visualization of tenant heatmap (redwood-console/plugins/canary-tenant-heatmap.ts) - Unit and integration tests that simulate heterogeneous tenant mixes (tests/test_headroom.py, tests/integration/test_tenant_quanta.yaml) - Docs and runbook describing tuning knobs and migration steps (docs/canaries/headroom.md) Design notes: - Headroom estimator uses a Bayesian low-sample smoothing prior tuned for burst detection; it intentionally weights very recent microburst probes higher so transient saturation is visible within 30s windows. - Fingerprints are lightweight histograms (log-buckets) of observed concurrency/latency pairs with TTL-based decay to avoid stale isolation after cutovers. - Rollback quanta are fractional percentages (eg 5% -> 50% of rollout traffic for affected tenants) computed from estimated probability of tail degradation; they are conservative by default and increase only after repeated correlated probes. - Integration with rollout controller allows per-tenant canary gating: if tenant headroom score exceeds threshold, traffic for that tenant is diverted to stable model variant or previous release. Migration and rollout: - This is opt-in behind a feature flag and off by default. - Suggested pilot: enable for 5 high-variance tenants for one week, observe Console heatmap and canary alerts, then widen. Checklist: - [x] Headroom estimator implementation - [x] Microburst probe and probe scheduler - [x] Rollout controller integration and quanta computation - [x] Tests: unit + integration - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Console visualization work Notes on safety: defaults are intentionally conservative; sentinel will not trigger account-wide rollbacks without two corroborating probe cycles and a cross-signal agreement (latency tail and concurrency spike). Related: ENG-4590 (tenant isolation perf initiative), SUP-1287 (customer incident with tenant burst).

reviews: Lena Park: Really like the per-tenant fingerprinting. One question: how large can the in-memory fingerprint store grow under heavy tenancy? Can we add a hard cap?

Aisha Khanna: Added eviction + approximate LRU with TTL; typical memory footprint is ~80 bytes per tenant histogram, capped via charts/canary-values.yaml. Included benchmarks in tests showing 10k tenants within 64MB budget.
Devon Harris: The Bayesian prior parameters look aggressive — might produce false positives for noisy short-lived spikes. Can we back off sensitivity and prefer repeated confirmation?

Aisha Khanna: Adjusted initial prior scale and added requirement for two corroborating probe cycles before increasing quanta beyond 10%. Kept single-cycle alert path for on-call visibility but not automated rollback.
Marcus Li: Integration with rollout controller looks clean. Please ensure feature flag gating and a clear kill-switch for emergency rollback (ideally via existing release controller API).
Aisha Khanna: Feature flag added (ff/perf/tenant_headroom) and rollout controller exposes an immediate emergency-disable endpoint; documented in runbook.
Lena Park: CI flaked on integration job initially, reran and all green. Approving for merge.
